page.layout: One page of text, single column; running head at top with page number at top right; catchword-like phrase "vox Latina" at the lower right below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.p: פָּרְסָא, פַּרְסָא Ch. Tentorium, velum, aulæum, tegumentum.
פַּרְסְתָּא, פַּרְסָא Ch. Ungula, à Fissura, Planta pedis. Plur. פַּרְסָת, פַּרְסָן.
פַּרְס Ch. Merces, præmium, munus, פַּרְסֵי נְטַל Adducentes munus, h.e. tributum annuum, מִם ידוע בכל שנה ut R. David scribit, 2. Sam. 8. 3. 6.
פְּרִיסוּתָא Ch. Separatio, Levit. 1. 8. in Jon. & cap. 3. v. 3.
Syr. Modus, Omni modo ad Phil. 1. 18.

Chal. Parsa, Parasanga, Milliare, Leuca. Plural. פַּרְסִי, פַּרְסִין Exo. 12. 31. Num. 21. 36. in Targ. Jonath. Ab hac voce פַּרְסָה scribit Drus. in Animadversi: lib. 1. c. 44. sibi deductam videri Latinam Parasanga, spatium mensuræ Persicæ. Adducit ibidem Franciscū Junium, qui existimat vocem esse corruptā in nostris libris, scribendúmque Parasangara: vult enim ita dici, quòd tantū spatii contineret, quantū Paras, h.e. eques angarus (ut ipse explicat) uno die coficere potest. Hæc opinio autem Drusio probabilis nō est, quòd Paras pro equite dictio sit Hebraica; Angarus autem Persica: copositio verò talis ex voce Persica & Hebraica nō fit consueta. At verò simpliciter vox videtur esse Persica. Nam פרסך ipsis Milliare significat. Sic enim Tavasius, Gen. 35. 16. & 48. 7. vocē Hebream כברה quam Milliare, omnes fere interpretes exponūt, reddit, quam vocem eam ipsam esse, à qua

page.notes: Hebrew, Syriac and Chaldean words are only approximately transcribed; the Syriac lines (Portio, Idem, Modus) are rendered as best read. Several Hebrew/Aramaic forms are uncertain and not marked individually. The word "vox Latina" at the foot is a catchword.
